structuredContent.row_meaning: 103 row(s) over 97 distinct lock identity(ies). AN IDENTITY IS NOT AN OBJECT: it is (name, scope, kind) where `name` is the SPELLING of the operand at an acquisition site, so one object reached by two spellings is two rows, and one spelling reached from unrelated types is one row. Of those 97 identities, 45 are THIS repository's and 52 belong to a vendored submodule (extern/llama.cpp), 0 declared in a file this index could not resolve. Quote origin.first_party as the count of the repository's own lock IDENTITIES — never as its mutex count. The field is still spelled `distinct_mutexes` for compatibility and holds that identity count, including other repositories'; `rows` is the un-collapsed row count. 18 identity(ies) are MEMBER expressions (bridge->tasks_mutex_, bridge.tasks_mutex_, buf_ctx->global_ctx->mutex, context.mutex …), so each names a struct or class member that THIS LAYER does not model — to enumerate those objects, dossier the owning type and read its members. The remaining 57 ARE separately identifiable: `dossier(<name>, kind='variable')` returns each one's type and every declaration site, which is enough to state that they are distinct objects.
structuredContent.nesting_meaning: 12 distinct two-lock holding(s) over 26 call site(s). Quote 12: each row is an ORDERED pair (outer taken first) and `sites` says how many call sites produce it, so the site total counts evidence, not nestings. A deadlock risk is two sites taking the SAME pair in OPPOSITE orders; compare the pairs, because the database reports observations and makes no deadlock claim. 8 pair(s) have resolved_sites=0 — every site resting on a call whose receiver was never verified — so do not quote those as confirmed. The full per-site list is lock_nestings in the query library.

## Mutexes in entropic

Querying the index's lock inventory (`search corpus=locks`) returns **103 rows over 97 distinct lock identities** (identity = `(name, scope, kind)` at an acquisition site — not 97 physical mutex objects; see confidence discussion below).

**Origin split:** 45 identities belong to this repository (`src/`, `include/`, `tests/`); 52 belong to the vendored `extern/llama.cpp` submodule.

### First-party mutexes (repo-owned, by class)

| Mutex | Owning class | File | Acquisitions |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adapter_mutex_` | `AdapterManager` | `src/inference/adapter_manager.cpp:212` | 11 |
| `auth_mutex_` | `MCPAuthorizationManager` | `src/mcp/mcp_authorization.cpp` | 10 |
| `registry_mutex_` | `GrammarRegistry` | `src/inference/grammar_registry.cpp` | 9 |
| `key_mutex_` | `MCPKeySet` | `src/mcp/mcp_key_set.cpp` | 8 |

| `mutex_` | `SqliteDatabase` | `src/storage/database.cpp` | 7 |

| `mtp_mutex_`, `seq_id_mutex_` | `LlamaCppBackend` | `src/inference/llama_cpp_backend.cpp` | 3, 2 |
| `mutex_` | `ToolCallHistory` (shared_mutex) | `src/mcp/tool_call_history.cpp` | 3 (+1 plain-mutex row on the same object) |
| `pending_mutex_`, `attempt_boundary_mutex_`, `critique_cbs_mutex_`, `result_mutex_` | `ConstitutionalValidator` | `src/core/constitutional_validator.cpp` | 3, 2, 2, 2 (5 distinct mutex members in one class) |

| `mutexes_[idx]` | `HookRegistry` (shared+plain, array) | `src/core/hook_registry.cpp` | 2+2 |
| `pending_mutex_` | `SSETransport` | `src/mcp/transport_sse.cpp` | 2 |
